message.content: Existing fusion research has benefited society by advancing high-temperature superconductors, plasma diagnostics, and advanced materials that now support medicine, transportation, and power systems. Neutron irradiation studies from fusion facilities improved understanding of reactor materials, aiding safer nuclear waste management and better shielding designs. Compact plasma experiments also strengthened computational fluid dynamics tools used in aerospace and climate modeling. Fusion-driven isotope production has explored medical tritium supplies, while related magnet technologies supported MRI and magnetic separation. Even if commercial fusion remains distant, its spillovers, iritic, clearly demonstrate tangible public value.
